nodes.title: Endpoint storage at rest
nodes.summary: Disks on laptops, desktops, and phones. A lost or stolen powered-off device exposes plaintext unless the volume is encrypted.

nodes.title: Data in transit
nodes.summary: Traffic across the internet, public Wi-Fi, and remote-admin paths. An on-path observer can read or alter cleartext.

nodes.title: Cloud data at rest
nodes.summary: Object stores, managed disks, and backups. Default storage encryption without separate key custody still fails with the account.

nodes.title: Plaintext on a lost device
nodes.summary: A lost or stolen endpoint yields work data, secrets, or key-adjacent files because the disk was unencrypted or the recovery key sat beside the device.
nodes.severityBasis: Default triage is high because a stolen laptop is common and the disk holds whatever the operator used. FDE does not stop a logged-in malware session.

nodes.title: On-path interception
nodes.summary: An observer on the network path reads or alters traffic that used HTTP, cleartext admin, or a broken TLS setup.
nodes.severityBasis: Default triage is high because cleartext remote admin and bulk HTTP expose credentials and change commands. Impact tracks what the channel carries.

nodes.title: Cloud plaintext at rest
nodes.summary: Object stores, disks, or backups keep data readable, or encryption keys sit in the same account as the ciphertext, so a stolen volume or hijacked role yields the data.
nodes.severityBasis: Default triage is high because cloud disks and buckets outlive any one server. Blast radius is the classified data in that store, not the compute instance.

nodes.title: Full-disk encryption
nodes.summary: Confirm FDE is on for every work endpoint, with a strong algorithm and recovery keys stored off the device.

nodes.title: TLS and SSH in transit
nodes.summary: Use modern TLS for internet traffic and SSH for remote admin. Cleartext HTTP and unencrypted remote shells are not acceptable on sensitive systems.

nodes.title: Cloud KMS key custody
nodes.summary: Encrypt cloud data at rest with a KMS or BYOK design. Do not leave keys in the same breach domain as the ciphertext.

nodes.title: Hardware-backed encryption keys
nodes.summary: Keep encryption keys in TPM, a self-encrypting drive, or an HSM so host memory and malware see less key material. This is not a hardware wallet.

nodes.title: Encryption
nodes.summary: Protect confidentiality when keys are managed on purpose across data at rest and in transit. Algorithms do not fix weak custody or cleartext channels.

nodes.title: Full-disk encryption
nodes.summary: Enable FDE on endpoints that store work data so lost or stolen devices do not expose plaintext at rest.

nodes.title: Hardware encryption
nodes.summary: TPM, self-encrypting drives, and HSMs keep encryption keys out of host memory when they are deployed and managed correctly.

nodes.title: Encryption in transit
nodes.summary: Data crossing networks uses TLS, SSH, or a VPN as appropriate. Cleartext remote admin and bulk HTTP are unacceptable for sensitive systems.

nodes.title: Cloud data encryption
nodes.summary: Encrypt cloud data in transit and at rest, with keys in a KMS or BYOK design, not default storage alone.
